official_last_added_basis: Datacurve changelog: GPT-6 Astra (all efforts) added 2026-09-03; its trials finished 2026-09-01. The 2026-09-22 generated_at is a site re-export with no new runs.
notes: The official board has added no model since 3 Sep 2026 (GPT-6 Astra; its runs finished on 1 Sep). The page was re-exported on 22 Sep with no new runs. Datacurve's CEO has said the team is building the next version of DeepSWE.

Epoch AI's review of 7 Sep 2026 rated DeepSWE 1.1 'flawed': it found grading defects in 23 of 113 tasks, mostly hidden tests colliding with tests the agent wrote. Tokenless separately documented 70 ways a submission can rewrite test outcomes. Treat differences of a few points with care.

Lab claims are run by the lab, on its own harness, effort settings and trial count. They are not directly comparable with the official runs (mini-swe-agent, 4 passes over 113 tasks). The harness is listed on every row; a few labs say Datacurve ran the evaluation for them (xAI for Grok 4.7).
Independent runs: Mercor (mini-swe-agent, 500 steps, 2-hour limit, 3 passes), Artificial Analysis (Grok Build harness), Fireworks (Kimi K3 at three effort levels) and entrpi (MiniMax M3).

Costs are per task in USD. The official page and its JSON file disagree for 19 of 70 configurations; this tracker shows the page's figure and records the file's in the row notes. Lab costs are the lab's own and are only shown where the lab published them.
Mercor shows no date for each model, so its results appear in the charts and table but not on the timeline.
A number is included only when it was read at the source that published it. Figures that appear only on aggregator sites are left out; the research log in research/ lists each one and why.
Anthropic has published no DeepSWE 1.1 score for Claude Haiku 5.5 (Mercor's independent run is the only one). There is no GPT-6.1 Luna: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Sol only.
